newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds close stronger on weak data, firm dlr.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds close stronger on weak data, firm dlr.

text.p: Canadian bonds retreated from early highs but still managed to close stronger on Friday, benefitting from weaker-than-expected U.S. producer price index data and strength in the Canadian dollar, analysts said.

"It looks like really we're just following through the momentum that we saw after this morning's release of the PPI data. They were very soft figures," said Rich Wylie, fixed-income economist with TD Securities Inc.
Canada's 30-year bond rose C$0.67 to C$114.42 to yield 6.812 percent. The U.S. 30-year benchmark bond rose 17/32 to yield 6.53 percent.
The spread between the benchmark bonds widened to 28 basis points from 24 basis points on Thursday.
Both Canadian and U.S. fixed-income markets were firmer this morning following a report that the U.S. January PPI fell 0.3 percent. Economists surveyed by Reuters had expected a 0.3 percent rise.

"That really does suggest that all of the growth we've seen recently in the U.S. economy has yet to result in measurable inflation pressures," said Wylie. "Clearly with inflationary pressures at bay, that's got to be good news for bonds."

Analysts said Canadian bonds also benefited from strength in the Canadian dollar during the session. The Canadian dollar closed stronger on Friday at C$1.3490 (US$0.7413) from Thursday's close at C$1.3512 (US$0.7401).
Bond trading activity was heavy in the morning but light in the afternoon, with the U.S. bond market closing early ahead of the U.S. President's Day holiday on Monday, analysts said.
Canadian fixed-income markets will remain open on Monday but activity is expected to be light with the U.S. market closed and the federal budget on Tuesday.
In other prices, the Government of Canada's 7.0 percent bond due 2006 rose C$0.30 to C$106.30 to yield 6.132 percent.
The U.S. 10-year bond rose 10/32 to yield 6.27 percent. The negative spread between the bonds widened to 14 basis points from 13 basis points at Thursday's close.
The three-month cash T-bill traded with a yield of 2.85 percent against the U.S. bill which yielded 5.09 percent.
